meta.source: U.S. Department of Energy final rules for consumer water heaters (89 FR, May 6, 2024: storage; 89 FR, December 26, 2024: gas-fired instantaneous) and DOE FEMP
meta.notes: DOE estimates lifetimes from national survey data (RECS and the American Housing Survey) with a survival function. For storage tanks DOE's 2024 average is about 15 years; its 2010 rule, ENERGY STAR and DOE FEMP use 13 years; AHRI assumes 10 to 13 years (as quoted in the 2024 rule). We use 13 as the typical value and 10 to 15 as the range. For tankless units DOE publishes an average of about 20 years and no range, so low, typical and high are all 20 until a primary source gives a range. Adjustments for water hardness, maintenance and anode replacement are Hot Water Math editorial assumptions, not measured data, and /methodology says so. costGuideViews: popular cost guides from the US top results for "how long does a water heater last", opened 2026-11-14; shown only for comparison (CLAUDE.md §8), never used as our value.

rheem.source: Rheem, Water Heater Lifespan: When to Repair vs. Replace (March 25, 2026): tank units typically last 8–12 years; tankless 15–20+ years with proper care; maintenance: flush the tank annually, replace the anode rod every 3–4 years, aim for 40–60 psi; replace when a repair costs more than 50% of a new unit
